title: How Multiple Births Can Accelerate A Mother’s Biological Age - Nautilus
gist: A Harvard Medical School review of studies using wearables, blood tests, epigenetic clocks and brain imaging finds pregnancy appears to speed biological aging, which slows again postpartum.

insights.claim: Evidence is mixed on whether child-bearing aids longevity or accelerates aging, and a new review tries to reconcile this.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Context for the longevity and women's health research debate.
insights.locator: There's some evidence that child-bearing benefits longevity

insights.claim: Two Harvard Medical School geneticists reviewed studies measuring women's biological age via wearables, blood tests, epigenetic clocks and brain imaging.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.locator: Two geneticists from Harvard Medical School

insights.claim: Pregnancy seems to speed up the biological clock, but it slows back down postpartum.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Suggests aging acceleration is partly reversible, relevant to biological-age clocks and women's health.
